query: What product attributes are associated with higher satisfaction scores?

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Clean, well-separated categorical segmentation of products (coffee/tea, snacks, pet food, etc.). An external attribute that can be grouped and compared against satisfaction to reveal which categories score higher.

per_column.name: flavor_taste_quality
per_column.rationale: Ordinal, interpretable taste-quality rating (excellent/good/acceptable/poor/off_flavor). A product attribute that plausibly associates with satisfaction. Some overlap with the satisfaction focus, but taste quality is a distinct describable attribute, not a restatement of the overall score.

per_column.name: flavor_intensity_balance
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categories (well_balanced, too_mild, too_strong) describing a concrete sensory attribute that can be segmented on and compared to satisfaction. 'not_applicable' is a reasonable bucket for non-flavor products.

per_column.name: product_effectiveness
per_column.rationale: Well-separated categories (works_as_claimed, partially_effective, no_effect, adverse_effect) capturing a distinct product attribute; a strong, interpretable candidate driver of satisfaction.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Categories are interpretable, but repurchase intent is essentially an outcome/proxy of satisfaction rather than an external product attribute. Correlating it with satisfaction is near-tautological, not an informative attribute-level relationship, and it is heavily NULL (~46%).

per_column.name: purchase_motivation
per_column.rationale: Interpretable segments (dietary need, curiosity, gifting, price-seeking) describing an external reviewer-context variable that can be compared against satisfaction. High NULL rate (~46%) weakens it, but the categories support meaningful segmentation.

judge.rationale: Most columns are external, interpretable, well-separated categorical attributes that a human can group on and compare against satisfaction, directly serving the 'what attributes drive satisfaction' query (product_category, flavor_taste_quality, flavor_intensity_balance, product_effectiveness are strong). repeat_purchase_intent is a satisfaction proxy/outcome rather than an attribute, so it partly restates the focus. Several columns carry substantial NULL/not_applicable mass, which limits comparison in subsets, but no column is opaque or a bare score. As a set, the columns support solid interpretable relationship discovery.
